title: Degreewise partial inversion preserves the diagonal nerve of a cofibrant pair
statement: Fix a small set $O$. Use the fixed-object model structure on simplicial categories on $O$ and functors fixing $O$ from [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model], for the $O\times O$-sorted algebraic theory of associative composition and identities. Weak equivalences and fibrations are weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations on each mapping simplicial set. Cofibrant means that the map from the identity-only category on $O$ has the left lifting property against every mappingwise trivial Kan fibration. Use simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $v:V\to B$ be a cofibration between cofibrant objects in this fixed-object model structure. Define $G(V)$ by groupoid-completing the ordinary category of degree-$q$ arrows of $V$ in every degree $q$, adjoining formal inverses and imposing inverse and composition relations; simplicial operators are induced by the universal properties. Let $B[V^{-1}]=B\amalg_VG(V)$, the ordinary pushout in fixed-object simplicial categories. For a simplicial category $T$ on $O$, put $B(T)_{p,q}=\coprod_{x_0,\ldots,x_p\in O}\prod_{r=1}^p T(x_{r-1},x_r)_q$; the first-direction operators compose or omit arrows and insert identities, and the second-direction operators are those of the mapping sets. Empty products are singletons. Its diagonal classifying nerve is $NT=\operatorname{diag}B(T)$. The canonical map $NB\to N(B[V^{-1}])$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. There is no hypothesis that any arrow in the image of $\pi_0V\to\pi_0B$ is invertible, and no Kan, connectedness, or nonemptiness hypothesis.

source.place: Dwyer–Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Proposition 10.2 and its proof, printed p.281; localization is 10.1, strong cofibration means a cofibration between cofibrant objects, and the nerve is 1.4(vi). Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy theorem.
